findings.text: The fail fixture's confinement breach is demonstrated via the FakeContainerDriver (the documented evidence path); a literal '/' mount would be rejected by real docker as a hard error rather than surfacing the breach. Non-blocking: grading is proven by fixtures plus selftest; a mount like /host covering /host/etc/shadow would be both a genuine breach and docker-runnable for a live demo.
Reference honesty rests on require_runtime being unit-tested to fail loud when no runtime is detected, which is deterministic regardless of docker presence on the build host.

summary: B17 (WARP-0317, sandbox/isolation reference runner) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review: gate GREEN, both fixtures correct (pass exit 0 with six checks both directions; fail exit 1 naming CONFINEMENT BREACH on /etc/shadow), 6/6 one-line mutations to classify/confine/grade caught, no rubber-stampable path (a no-checks journey and a malformed check are named errors), capabilities status reference is honest (no container surface in the warp gate; live path fails loud absent a runtime), generic, ASCII, stdlib-only, both capabilities.yaml copies byte-identical. Post-review closure applied before ship: removed a decorative '# ---' comment divider to comply with the no-double-hyphen house rule (no behavior change). proof_digest recomputed via validate.py.
